newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PITCHER'S PINCH HIT LIFTS MARLINS PAST BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PITCHER'S PINCH HIT LIFTS MARLINS PAST BRAVES.

text.p: Pitcher Dennis Cook put his perfect record as a pinch hitter on the line Friday and delivered a RBI single in the 12th inning to lift the Florida Marlins to a 3-2 victory over the Atlanta Braves.
The win was the fifth for the Marlins in six games against the Braves this season and moved them within 5 1/2 games of first-placed Atlanta in the NL East Division.
Charles Johnson led off the 12th with a double off reliever Mike Cather (0-2) and Marlins manager Jim Leyland used Gregg Zaun, his last position player, as a pinch runner.

With Zaun on third, Leyland turned to Cook, who was 3-for-3 in pinch-hit situations, including a home run in a game last Friday. Cook again came through, lining a single to right to score Zaun with the winning run.
The Florida bullpen pitched four scoreless innings and allowed just one hit. Jay Powell (2-2) worked the final 1 2/3 innings for the win.
The game matched aces Greg Maddux of the Braves and Florida's Kevin Brown.

Maddux, who was aiming to become the National League's first 16-game winner, allowed just one run and three hits in seven innings. Brown pitched eight innings and allowed two runs, one earned, and four hits while striking out nine.
In Pittsburgh, Larry Walker's second solo homer of the game -- a two-out blast in the ninth inning -- lifted the Colorado Rockies to a 7-6 victory over the Pirates.
It was the fifth multiple-homer game of the season for Walker, who leads the National League with 32 home runs.
Ricardo Rincon (4-5) retired the first two batters in the ninth before Walker hit a 2-2 pitch over the centre field wall to snap a 6-6 tie. Walker also homered in the first inning.
Steve Reed pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings for the win.
In Chicago, Todd Zeile and Todd Hollandsworth combined for five hits, seven RBI and five runs scored as the Los Angeles Dodgers withstood five homers to beat the Cubs 13-9.
Zeile had two hits, including a three-run homer, drove in four runs and scored three times. Hollandsworth doubled twice, singled, scored twice and knocked in three runs.
Every member of the Dodgers' starting lineup, including pitcher Hideo Nomo, was on base at least twice as Los Angeles banged out 20 hits in its seventh straight win.
Ryne Sandberg, Brian McRae, Sammy Sosa, Doug Glanville and Kevin Orie homered for the Cubs, losers of nine in a row.

In Cincinnati, newly-acquired Wilson Alvarez allowed three hits over six innings to win his San Francisco debut and Jeff Kent went 3-for-4 with three RBI as the Giants held on for an 8-7 victory over the Reds to remain tied with the Dodgers atop the NL West.
Alvarez (1-0), acquired Thursday with pithers Roberto Hernandez and Danny Darwin from the Chicago White Sox, allowed five runs with four walks and seven strikeouts.
Hernandez also made his Giants' debut and gave up a two-run homer to Reggie Sanders in the eighth. But Rod Beck worked the ninth for his league-leading 33rd save.
In Houston, Edgardo Alfonzo's two-run double highlighted a four-run 10th inning as the New York Mets rallied to beat the Astros 8-5.
The Mets snapped a 4-4 tie in the 10th by scoring four times against a pair of Astros relievers.

After Lance Johnson and Bernard Gilkey walked, Todd Hundley delivered an RBI single for a 5-4 lead. Alfonzo, who made a costly throwing error that allowed Houston to tie the game in the bottom of ninth, then redeemed himself with a two-run double into the left-field corner.

In Montreal, Joey Hamilton tossed a four-hitter on only 83 pitches for his fifth straight win and first complete game in more than a year as the San Diego Padres rolled to an 8-2 victory over the Expos.
Chris Gomez tied a career high with four hits and drove in three runs for San Diego, which improved to 15-7 since the All-Star break.
Hamilton (9-3) made only one mistake, allowing Doug Strange's two-run homer in the fifth. By then, the Padres had provided him with a 7-0 cushion.

In Philadelphia, Garrett Stephenson tossed eight strong innings and Gregg Jefferies had two hits and two RBI to lead the Phillies to their season-high fourth straight win, a 4-1 triumph over the St Louis Cardinals.

Stephenson (5-5) gave up a run and nine hits with six strikeouts and no walks. Ricky Bottalico, the subject of numerous trade rumours before the Thursday deadline, got the final three outs for his 20th save in 23 opportunities.
Mark McGwire, acquired by St Louis from Oakland Thursday, went 0-for-3 in his National League debut.
